title: attest: OpenSSH cross-validation claimed but never run
description:
tests/attest/test_attest.py:5-9 says each case's `openssh_accepts` "is the verdict of OpenSSH's regress/misc/ssh-verify-attestation (openssh-portable 26b1363, linked against libfido2 1.14)". DESIGN.md:534-535 says the tool "is cross-validated against OpenSSH's regress/misc/ssh-verify-attestation". Neither is true yet. vouch-ey47.15 notes that building the oracle needs libfido2-dev, which is not installed. There is no /usr/include/fido.h and no ssh-verify-attestation binary anywhere on this host. All 14 test_openssh_reference_verdicts cases skip. The 14 `openssh_accepts` booleans are hand predictions written down as if they were observed output.

This finding is separate from running the oracle, which vouch-ey47.15 tracks. It is about provenance text that is false now and stays false if ey47.15 slips. A reviewer reading the docstring or DESIGN.md will believe that the format assumptions shared by make_fixtures.py and the tool were independently checked. Those assumptions are the CBOR-wrapped authData, reserved u32 plus string, and clientDataHash = SHA-256(challenge). I checked them by reading openssh-portable source (ssh-verify-attestation.c:99-116 and sk-usbhid.c:329-338/896), not by execution. Because both sides encode the same reading, these tests cannot catch a shared misreading.

Fix: until the oracle is run, reword the docstring to "expected verdict of ... (predicted from source, not yet run; see vouch-ey47.15)" and DESIGN.md to "is to be cross-validated". Restore the current wording when ey47.15 closes.
notes: Done: tests/attest/test_attest.py docstring now says predicted from source, not yet run (vouch-ey47.15). Remaining: DESIGN.md:534-535 'is to be cross-validated ... (vouch-ey47.15)' (docs unit, doc_changes). Close when applied.
